document.abstract: Film recording and reproducing equipment has recently been developed for the sound replacement program of the Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Studio. The completion of the program is of course indefinitely delayed because of the war situation, but the apparatus design had previously been brought to the stage of finished pilot models. Quality of product was the primary design criterion although it was found practicable to meet optimum quality requirements and at the same time keep cost and difficulty of installation and maintenance at a minimum. The apparatus integrates all the many developments that have long been standard practice in Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer motion picture sound production, and in addition provides many new features of additional value.
